title: Inducing primary brainstem gliomas in genetically engineered mice using RCAS/TVA retroviruses and Cre/loxP recombination
protocol: Turn on the biological safety cabinet and disinfect gloved hands with 70% ethanol.
Disinfect the work surface with 70% ethanol.
Gather Eppendorf tubes (2 per plasmid), T25 flasks containing DF1 cells, transfection reagent X-tremeGENE™, RCAS-Cre, RCAS-Luc, RCAS-PDGFB, and RCAS-GFP plasmid stocks in 1.7 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Spray the exteriors of the gathered items with 70% ethanol and place inside the biological safety cabinet.
Label one Eppendorf tube with the plasmid name (e.g., RCAS-Cre).
Label another Eppendorf tube with “DMEM null” for each plasmid.
Ensure that T25 flasks are appropriately labeled.
Disinfect the DMEM null container exterior with 70% ethanol and place inside the biological safety cabinet when finished warming.
Aliquot 242.5 μL of DMEM null into each Eppendorf tube labeled “DMEM null”.
Add 7.5 μL of X-tremeGENE™ 9 into each Eppendorf tube containing DMEM
Add X-tremeGENE™ 9 directly to the DMEM.
Change pipette tips before moving on to the next Eppendorf tube.
Let the DMEM and X-tremeGENE™ 9 mixture incubate at 20°C–22°C for 5 min.
Aliquot 2.5 μg of each plasmid to its appropriate Eppendorf tube.
Add the DMEM and X-tremeGENE™ 9 mixture to each plasmid after the 5-min incubation period.
Mix each tube containing DMEM, X-tremeGENE™ 9, and plasmid by flicking for 10 s.
Let each tube containing DMEM, X-tremeGENE™ 9, and plasmid incubate at 20°C–22°C for 20 min.
Add each DMEM, X-tremeGENE™ 9, and plasmid mixture to its appropriate T25 flask.
Add the mixture dropwise to the cells in the flask.
Place the T25 flasks of cells back into the incubator.
Harvest DF1 cells transfected with RCAS-GFP when they are confluent and between passages 3 to 20 after transfection.
Verify GFP expression in harvested DF1 cells using a fluorescent microscope before proceeding with further steps.
Warm DF1 media in a warm water or pebble bath at 37°C for 30 min to 1 h.
Find a Styrofoam box or cooler and fill it with ice.
Turn on the biological safety cabinet and disinfect gloved hands with 70% ethanol.
Disinfect the work surface with 70% ethanol.
Ensure the workspace is stocked with conical tubes, serological pipettes, micropipette tips, lab markers, tissue culture flasks, etc.
Place prewarmed DF1 media inside the biological safety cabinet.
Place prewarmed PBS inside the biological safety cabinet.
Place prewarmed 0.25% trypsin inside the biological safety cabinet.
Remove spent media from cells using aspiration.
Wash cells with 5 ml of PBS.
Trypsinize cells with 0.7 ml of 0.25% trypsin for a T25 flask or 1 ml for a T75 flask.
Incubate cells at 39°C for 5 min until detached.
Neutralize the 0.25% trypsin inside the flask with DF1 media.
Triturate the cells three times and passage at the desired ratio.
Place the flasks containing the newly passaged cells into the incubator.
Do not discard the flask(s) of cells from which the passaged cells were taken.
Determine the cell counts.
For manual cell counting, use trypan blue solution and a C-Chip disposable hemocytometer kit.
Follow the instructions provided by the kit to calculate the cell counts for the cells of the cell lines that will be used for mouse injections.
Add together the cells transfected with RCAS-Cre, RCAS-Luc, and RCAS-PDGFB in a 1:1:1 mixture.
To calculate the volume of cells of each group needed to reach this ratio, divide the smallest cell count out of all the groups by the cell count of the group of interest.
Multiply that value by the volume of media remaining in the flask containing the cells of the group with the smallest cell count.
Transfer the appropriate volume of cells of each group into a 50 mL conical tube.
Spin the cells in a centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Check that a pellet has formed.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in DF1 media.
Calculate the volume of DF1 media needed to resuspend the cells by dividing the total number of cells by 100,000.
Place the cells on ice.
Note: The harvested cells should be kept on ice for a maximum of 1 hour.
Clean a laminar-flow hood with disinfectant.
Retrieve all necessary materials and the mice to be injected.
Clean the inside of a Hamilton syringe with de-ionized water.
Sedate mouse pups using hypothermia by placing them on ice covered with aluminum foil until they stay still.
Withdraw 1 × 10^5 virus-producing DF1 cells resuspended in 1 μL of cell media using a Hamilton syringe.
Inject 1 μL of the resuspended DF1 cells into the brainstem of a mouse pup by positioning the needle tip between the ears and tilting the syringe at a 15° angle.
Drive the needle about 2 mm below the skin to enter the injection site.
Thaw luciferin solution in a heating block.
Remove the thawed luciferin from the heating block and place it in a cooler of ice.
Bring the thawed luciferin to the IVIS Lumina III In Vivo Imaging System.
Start-up the IVIS Lumina III.
Open the LivingImage 4.5 software.
Log into the appropriate user account.
Click “initialize” to warm-up the IVIS Lumina III.
Set up the work area.
Gather all necessary materials while the IVIS Lumina III is initializing.
Ensure the oxygen concentrator, isoflurane vaporizer, and mouse induction chamber are properly set up with tubes and connections secured.
Check that the isoflurane level in the vaporizer is full or near full.
Turn on the oxygen concentrator and isoflurane vaporizer.
Adjust the flow rate of isoflurane between 2.5 and 3% v/v.
Weigh the mice and record their weights.
Place the mice in the induction chamber until they are anesthetized.
Remove hair from the mice using nair and a cotton swab.
Apply nair to the head of the mouse with a cotton swab.
Return the mouse to the induction chamber for 3–5 minutes.
Remove as much of the nair and loose hair as possible using a wet cotton swab.
Thoroughly rinse the mouse’s head with water and iodine to prevent burns.
Adjust the IVIS Lumina III settings as needed.
Make sure no lens is attached to the inside top of the imager.
Remove any present lens by pulling downward.
Set the field of view to “D”.
Ensure that “XFOV-24” is unchecked.
Check both “luminescence” and “photograph” boxes.
Position the nose cones correctly inside the IVIS Lumina III.
Set the exposure time to “60 s”.
Inject 1 to 3 mice with 15 mg/mL luciferin via intraperitoneal injection.
Calculate the volume of luciferin solution equal to 10 μL per gram of body weight for each mouse.
Draw the appropriate volume of luciferin solution into an insulin syringe.
Remove any bubbles on the inside of the syringe by flicking and slowly dispensing the solution.
Place the insulin syringe needle tip at the lower abdomen of the mouse, very slightly angle the syringe.
Carefully push the needle into the mouse.
Dispense the appropriate volume of luciferin into the mouse by slowly depressing the syringe plunger.
Carefully remove the needle from the mouse.
Place the mouse back into the induction chamber and record the time of injection.
Wait 15 minutes after injecting each mouse.
Position the mouse inside the in vivo bioluminescent imaging system chamber a couple of minutes before the 15-minute wait period ends.
Begin the luminescence imaging by clicking “Acquire”.
Make sure the door to the IVIS Lumina III is closed before clicking "acquire".
Save the image file.
Remove the sedated mice and return them to their cage(s).
Close the software.
Turn off the oxygen concentrator.
Turn off the isoflurane vaporizer.
Anesthetize mice using isoflurane vaporizer set between 2.5 and 3% v/v flow rate.
Place anesthetized mouse on the X-Rad 225cx stage in a prone position.
Acquire orthogonal X-ray images with fluoroscopy using 40 kVp, 2.5 mA x-rays filtered through 2 mm aluminum.
Irradiate mice with 225 kVp, 13 mA x-rays filtered through 0.3 mm copper using a 15 × 40 mm rectangular radiation field.
Deliver right and left lateral fields to the irradiation target area.
Remove tumor and place in PBS.
Cut tumor into small pieces and transfer to a 15 mL tube.
Filter papain solution to make it sterile.
Vortex the filtered papain solution, incubate at 37°C for a few minutes, then vortex again.
Use a 0.2 μm filter for sterile filtration of papain solution.
Incubate filtered papain solution at room temperature for 30 min to activate (active for 1 h).
Aspirate PBS off the tumor tissue.
Resuspend tumor tissue in 5 ml papain + 30 μL DNase.
Triturate 30× with a 5 mL pipet.
Incubate for 15 min at 37°C.
During this incubation time, prepare and sterile filter the ovomucoid solution.
Use a 0.2 μm filter for sterile filtering.
Add 2 mL of ovo solution, then invert.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 162 × g.
Aspirate supernatant.
Add 500 μL of ovo to pellet, then triturate with P1000 30×.
Add 5 mL Neurocult (basal).
Centrifuge for 5 min at 48 × g.
Collect supernatant, if desired, into a 50 mL conical tube.
Repeat steps 50–53, two more times (not necessary).
Resuspend pellet in Neurocult complete media and strain through a cell strainer to remove clumps of cells and tissue that did not dissociate.
Combine with supernatant collected from the three spins if desired (will contain more cells, but will also contain dead cells and debris).
Spin again at 162 × g for 5 min.
Count cells and place in appropriate vessel.
Cut mouse tail about 2–3 mm long and place in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 500 μL of Lysis buffer and 8 μL Proteinase K solution, mix well.
Incubate in 55°C–60°C oven for 3 h.
Vortex for 10 s and spin for 3 min at 13,000 × g in centrifuge.
Add 1,000 μL of 100% EtOH and mix by inverting three times.
Spin for 5 min at 13,000 × g in centrifuge.
Pour out supernatant and air-dry DNA for 30 min.
Add 200 μL–300 μL dH2O to each DNA tube.
Incubate in 55°C–60°C oven for 20 min.
Vortex for 10 s and spin DNA for a second in centrifuge, then add 1.5 μL–2 μL for PCR.
Store DNA at 4°C.
Add appropriate mix and DNA to PCR vials.
Run PCR vials in thermocycler.
Prepare 1% agarose in TAE buffer in an Erlenmeyer flask.
Microwave the flask for 70 s.
If the agarose has not fully dissolved, microwave the flask for an additional 25 s.
Add 8–10 μL of SYBR safe to the agarose solution.
Add well combs to the gel mold.
Gently pour the agarose SYBR safe solution into the mold.
Cool the gel for 40 min or place at 4°C to cool more rapidly.
Carefully remove the combs.
Remove the gel from the mold.
Prepare PCR vials for gel electrophoresis.
Add 8 μL of 5× orange gel loading dye to each PCR vial.
Flick the vials to mix the contents.
Spin down the vials to bring liquids to the bottom.
Place the gel in an electrophoresis chamber filled with 1× TAE buffer.
Add 15 μL of a ladder solution to the first well of each row.
Add 12 μL of the PCR vial contents to each well.
Run the gel at 120 V for 25 min.
Extract genomic DNA from flow-sorted primary glioma cells using PicoPure DNA extraction kit.
Design hexachloro-fluorescein and fluorescein amidite-conjugated TaqMan probes.
Dilute genomic DNA to 26 ng/μL.
Prepare master mix for droplet digital PCR.
Generate droplets using the QX200 Automated Droplet Generator according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Perform PCR amplification on generated droplets.
Analyze data using QuantaSoft™ Software (Bio-Rad).
